plan.expected_observation: For both load directions, low-load displacement exceeds 0.006 m with selected tendon tension at or below 0.005 N and positive slack; by the high stage the direction-appropriate tendon exceeds 0.05 N, its constraint residual is at most 5e-05 m, and the late stiffness ratio exceeds 1.5 while displacement stays below 0.025 m.
plan.fixed_conditions: Keep the frozen passive-response evaluator, prototype segment sections and cells, material defaults, equal angular tendon spacing, common full-span routing, and identical payout offsets across all four tendons. Treat mathematical screening as distinct from finite dynamic acceptance.
plan.hypothesis: A two-segment arm with four equally spaced full-span tendons and identical positive payout offsets will remain compliant and effectively slack at low loads, while the tendon on the extending side will engage under each opposite high-load bend, producing approximately symmetric progressive stiffness for plus-x and minus-x.
plan.interpretation: This is a new unmeasured structure designed to test delayed unilateral engagement, not a claim of task success. Fourfold symmetry is intended to remove a directional confounder; the common positive payout offset is the primary engagement-delay intervention.
plan.stopping_condition: Stop this design branch if it cannot produce a qualified unloaded state or bilateral delayed activation under current scoped analysis; otherwise proceed to candidate-bound mechanism diagnosis and then a matched physical evaluation before any validation replay.
plan.weakening_observation: Either unloaded or low-stage tendons are already taut, neither direction activates a tendon by the high stage, activation is strongly one-sided, the arm remains too stiff at low load, or high-load dynamics are unstable or exceed the displacement bound.
